a.name: Steel lock snap
a.desc: A crisp steel slide-lock snapping into place, with a tiny ring.
a.note: Slide lock 1 (a real metal slide lock, cut 4 ms in so its snap peaks at 5 ms) for the snap; a Kenney light steel impact, highpassed and 4 dB down, adds a short bright ring for the reward. Sheet: spike at 5 ms, gone by 150 ms. (Chosen over the Kenney metal latch, which three other groups already lead with.)

b.name: Wooden knock snap
b.desc: A crisp wooden knock with a small crack in it.
b.note: Woodcrack (1), a 40 ms dry crack, for the crisp top; the classic Wood Knock and a Kenney light wood tap give it a short hollow body (the crack alone is too thin to reach the loudness target).

c.name: Bright glass tink
c.desc: A tiny, bright tink, like a fingernail on a glass.
c.note: kenney light glass impact, original take

a.name: Dead metal clunk
a.desc: A blade clunking dully off armour, flat and lifeless.
a.note: Kenney medium metal impact pitched down 6 semitones and lowpassed at 1.4 kHz (all the ring and sparkle gone), over a dull hammer thump (fs-264879 third hit) for a blunt body. Steel family, the deflated twin of the steel snap.

b.name: Hollow wood tok
b.desc: A hollow wooden knock, pitched low, like hitting an empty crate.
b.note: Kenney medium wood impact pitched down 3 semitones and lowpassed at 2 kHz: a dead, hollow knock that says nothing landed.

c.name: Padded cloth bump
c.desc: A weak blow bumping into thick cloth, soft and deflated.
c.note: Medium Thud 1 (first take), lowpassed at 1.8 kHz, for a soft padded hit; a fabric flap right after it sells the limp follow-through. Sheet: thud at 7 ms, cloth noise until 120 ms.

a.name: Quick blade nick
a.desc: A fast, light steel slice, a small flick of a blade.
a.note: Kenney RPG knifeSlice2, only its sharp first 160 ms (hard metal onset at 4 ms, then a quick decay; the later swell is cut off). Lighter and shorter than the main strike.

b.name: Quick chop
b.desc: A quick chop that thuds into its target.
b.note: Kenney RPG chop, cut 45 ms in so it starts right on the bite (peak at 8 ms): wood body with a steel edge, cut tight.

c.name: Fist jab
c.desc: A quick gloved punch with a small whip of air.
c.note: Punching Impact Sound (third take, peak at 8 ms, mid-low body) plus a quiet small whip snap for speed.

a.name: Blade drawn
a.desc: A hilt click and a quick steel scrape as a blade comes out.
a.note: Kenney RPG drawKnife3 from 120 ms: its hilt click lands at 12 ms. The bright middle of drawKnife1 (the steel scrape) is laid in 8 ms later, raised so the scrape stays audible after the click.

b.name: Cloak rustle
b.desc: A quick cloak and cloth rustle as someone steps in.
b.note: Kenney RPG cloth2 from just before its main rustle: two cloth flicks, soft and grounded.

c.name: Buckle jingle step
c.desc: A boot step with a belt buckle clinking, gear being readied.
c.note: Kenney RPG beltHandle1 from its loudest clink (a ringing buckle) over a quiet Kenney wooden footstep.

a.name: Bone-cracking blow
a.desc: A heavy punch that cracks bone, with crunchy splinters after.
a.note: Bone Crack (1) crunch first (spike at 5 ms), Face Punch (3) under it for a dense, meaty body, Bone Crack (2) crackles trailing from 60 ms.

b.name: Splintering timber
b.desc: A heavy blow that splits old wood, splinters creaking after.
b.note: Old heavy door kick (low wood body and rattle) with the Hydraulic log splitter crack laid on its peak, and wood splinters creaking from 60 ms.

c.name: Stone shatter boom
c.desc: Stone breaking apart over a deep boom, rubble trickling down.
c.note: Stone Crumble 2 for the breaking rock and rubble, a Kenney pickaxe-on-rock hit (cut at 260 ms, before its metallic ring shows on the sheet) for a hard stony front, a deep hit for the burst and a low rumble tail.
